'''Terence Richard Wyatt''' (born 29 June 1957)<ref name="whoswho"/> {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}}<ref name=frs/> is a Professor in the [[School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Manchester|School of Physics and Astronomy]] at the [[University of Manchester]], UK.<ref name="scopus">{{Scopus id}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/T.R.Wyatt.1|title=Scientific publications of Terry Wyatt|publisher=[[INSPIRE-HEP]]|website=inspirehep.net}}</ref><ref name=off>{{Official URL}}</ref>

==Education==
Wyatt was educated at [[Landau Forte Academy QEMS|Queen Elizabeth's Grammar School, Tamworth]], [[Imperial College London]] (Bachelor of Science) and [[St Edmund Hall, Oxford]] where he was awarded a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in 1983 for research supervised by [[Robin Devenish]] at the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name="wyattphd">{{cite thesis |degree=DPhil |first=Terence Richard |last=Wyatt |title=A study of the production of b quarks in e<sup>+</sup>e<sup>−</sup> annihilation at high energies |publisher=University of Oxford |year=1983 |url=https://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/permalink/44OXF_INST/rl48sd/alma990121510700107026  |author-link=Terry Wyatt |oclc=863491161 |website=ox.ac.uk}}</ref><ref name="whoswho"/>

==Career and research==
Wyatt's conducts research in [[particle physics]] primarily on the [[D0 experiment|DØ experiment]] at the [[Tevatron]] proton-antiproton collider in [[Fermilab]] and on the [[ATLAS experiment]] at the [[Large Hadron Collider]] proton-proton collider in [[CERN]].<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1016/j.nima.2006.05.248| title = The upgraded DØ detector| journal = Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment| volume = 565| issue = 2| pages = 463–537| year = 2006| last1 = Abazov | first1 = V. He was one of three short-listed candidates for the position of CERN [[Director-general|Director General]] in 2014, with [[Fabiola Gianotti]] and Frank Linde.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1038/nature.2014.16287|title=Higgs hunter will be CERN's first female director|journal=Nature|year=2014|last1=Castelvecchi|first1=Davide|s2cid=124442791|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Wyatt was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2013|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2013]].<ref name=frs>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119110956/https://royalsociety.org/people/terry-wyatt-12571/|archive-date=2015-11-19|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/terry-wyatt-12571/|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|title=Professor Terry Wyatt FRS}}</ref> His certificate of election reads: {{centred pull quote|Terry Wyatt is an experimental particle physicist who is distinguished for a number of original and important contributions to the experimental verification of the Standard Model (SM). By combining unusual expertise in detector performance with exceptional insight into the topological features of different interaction dynamics, Wyatt has developed and implemented powerful new discriminants of signatures for the production of heavy quarks (b and t) and electroweak bosons (W and Z). His application of these techniques in electron-positron interactions (LEP at CERN) and in antiproton-proton interactions (TeVatron at Fermilab) has resulted in measurements of unprecedented precision. His experimental insight and innovation continue to underpin his work, most notably in his recent leadership as co-spokesperson of the D0 experiment at Fermilab. As new high quality data are taken, he continues to pursue measurements of SM observables with new sensitivity, based on the exploitation of the present luminosity regime at the TeVatron.<ref name=frs/>}}

Wyatt was also awarded the [[James Chadwick Medal and Prize]] from the [[Institute of Physics]] (IOP) in 2011.<ref name="chadwick">{{cite web |url=http://www.eps.manchester.ac.uk/about-us/features/chadwick-medal |title=Prof Terry Wyatt Receives Chadwick Medal |publisher=University of Manchester |archive-date=3 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140303055902/http://www.eps.manchester.ac.uk/about-us/features/chadwick-medal/ }}</ref>
